title: Identifiability of Child's Location
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted from the child's device can be used to identify the child's precise location, movements, and patterns of behavior, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily routine, school, home, and other locations.

title: Linkability of Location Data
description: GPS coordinates can be linked across time periods to create a detailed movement profile of the child, enabling correlation with other data sources to infer additional personal information about the child's activities and associations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Live GPS coordinates may be accessed by unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls, exposing the child's real-time location to malicious actors.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Continuous transmission of live GPS coordinates at regular intervals may exceed what is necessary for the intended purpose, collecting more location data than required and increasing privacy risk.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Processing of a child's location data may violate data protection regulations such as GDPR or COPPA, which impose strict requirements for handling children's personal data and require parental consent.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: Location data written to the datastore could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially revealing users' movement patterns and habits.

title: Location Data Tampering
description: Location data in the datastore could be altered, deleted, or corrupted by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity.

title: Individual Identification via Location Data
description: Stored location history could be used to identify specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.

title: Linkability of Location Data
description: Location data could be linked with other personal information or data sources, creating a comprehensive profile of individuals.

title: Identifiability through Location Tracking
description: Location pings transmitted from the Mobile App Backend can be used to identify and track individual users' movements, potentially revealing sensitive information about their habits, routines, and whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is personally identifiable and can be correlated with user identities

title: Linkability Across Data Sources
description: Location data from the backend could be linked with other data sources (e.g., user profiles, device IDs) to create comprehensive movement profiles, enabling detailed behavioral analysis.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be correlated

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: The Geofencing Engine may expose location data to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: System may have inadequate security controls

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The geofencing engine may collect more precise or frequent location data than necessary for zone entry/exit detection, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: System may not implement data minimization by design

title: Regulatory Compliance Issues
description: Location tracking and processing may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent mechanisms, data retention policies, and user rights are not implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements exist for location data processing

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Zone Definitions
description: Configured geofencing zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) stored in DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties, revealing sensitive location information about family members and their routines.
assumptions: Zone definitions contain personally identifiable location data that could be exploited for stalking or unwanted surveillance.

title: Linkability of Location Patterns
description: Zone definitions could be linked to specific individuals or their daily routines, enabling inference of family members' whereabouts and movement patterns over time.
assumptions: Zone definitions are associated with specific user accounts and could be correlated with other data sources.

title: Tampering with Geofencing Configurations
description: Unauthorized modification of zone definitions could lead to incorrect geofencing alerts, false privacy notifications, or manipulation of family monitoring capabilities.
assumptions: Attackers could gain access to DS2 and modify zone boundaries or alert settings.

title: Inference of Sensitive Locations
description: The Geofencing Engine could infer sensitive location information (e.g., home address, school location) from zone definitions, potentially exposing private information beyond intended use.
assumptions: P2 processes zone definitions in a way that could reveal location data to other system components or through side channels.

title: Usurpation of Zone Management Authority
description: Unauthorized users could potentially impersonate legitimate users to modify or access zone definitions, leading to privacy violations or false alerts.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms in P2 could be bypassed or compromised.

title: Linkability of Geofencing Data to Individuals
description: Arrival/departure notifications from the Geofencing Engine could be linked to specific individuals, potentially revealing movement patterns and associating them with specific locations or activities.
assumptions: The system logs or stores notification data that can be correlated with user identities

title: Identification of Individuals via Zone Entry/Exit
description: The geofencing notifications could be used to identify which individuals are entering or exiting specific zones, potentially revealing sensitive information about their whereabouts and activities.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE1) has access to notification data that can be correlated with user identities

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Location-based arrival/departure notifications could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive information about individuals' movements and activities.
assumptions: The data flow is not adequately protected, or the parent entity shares data with third parties

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Location Tracking
description: The geofencing and location tracking functionality may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding the collection and transmission of location data without proper consent or safeguards.
assumptions: The system does not have adequate consent mechanisms or data protection measures in place
uncertainty_note: Node selection based on general regulatory compliance concerns; specific regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction

title: Child Profile Linkability
description: The child's profile data (name, DOB, school) could be linked with other data sources or across systems to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially revealing patterns or associations that compromise privacy.
assumptions: Data is stored in multiple systems or shared with third parties

title: Child Identification Risk
description: The combination of name, date of birth, and school information in the child's profile could be used to uniquely identify the child, potentially exposing them to unwanted attention or tracking.
assumptions: Child's information is accessible to unauthorized parties

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Data
description: Sensitive child profile information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, improper access controls, or unauthorized sharing with third parties.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data protection measures

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Collecting comprehensive child profile data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) may exceed what is necessary for the geofencing functionality, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Data collection is not strictly limited to what is needed for the stated purpose

title: Account Usurpation
description: An attacker could compromise the parent's account and create or modify child profiles for children they should not have access to, potentially leading to unauthorized surveillance or data collection.
assumptions: Parent account credentials are compromised

title: Geofence Zone Data Disclosure
description: Geofence zone data (location boundaries) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, revealing the child's home, school, or other sensitive locations.
assumptions: Location data is stored or transmitted without adequate protection

title: Profile Creation Non-Repudiation
description: The parent may be unable to prove they created or modified the child's profile, which could lead to disputes about data accuracy or unauthorized modifications.
assumptions: No audit trail or logging of profile creation/modification activities

title: Unauthorized Data Leakage of Family Account Information
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could leak sensitive family account credentials, child profile data, and geofence zone information to unauthorized third parties through vulnerabilities in the backend system or insecure data transmission channels.
assumptions: Assumes backend has vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Unauthorized Modification of Child Profile and Geofence Data
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could allow unauthorized actors to modify child profile information or geofence zone settings, potentially leading to false location tracking or inappropriate access restrictions.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient authentication and authorization controls

title: Identification of Minors Through Profile and Location Data
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) could enable identification of children through their stored profiles, geofence patterns, and associated family account information, potentially exposing minors' identities and locations.
assumptions: Assumes data could be accessed or correlated by unauthorized parties

title: Unintended Consequences from Geofence Pattern Analysis
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) could lead to unintended consequences where geofence zone data reveals family routines, schedules, and behavioral patterns that could be exploited for stalking or targeted attacks.
assumptions: Assumes geofence data could be accessed and analyzed by third parties

title: Location data reveals child's sensitive locations
description: Location data collected from the child could reveal sensitive information such as home address, school, workplace, or frequent locations, making the child identifiable through their movement patterns.
assumptions: Location data is stored and accessible in a way that allows pattern analysis

title: Location data can be linked across contexts
description: Location data from different time periods or applications could be linked together to create a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and habits.
assumptions: Location data is retained over time and accessible across systems

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: Location data could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Access controls may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized access

title: Excessive location data collection
description: The system may collect more location data than necessary for the specific request (e.g., continuous tracking when only current location is needed, or collecting historical data beyond what's requested).
assumptions: Data collection policies may not align with the principle of data minimization

title: Unauthorized access to parent's account
description: If the parent's account credentials are compromised, unauthorized individuals could access the child's location data through the parent's account.
assumptions: Parent account security may be insufficient to prevent credential compromise

title: Location History Linkability to Individual
description: Stored location history can be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking of movements and activities over time.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify individuals and their movement patterns.

title: Location History Identifiability
description: Location patterns and history can be used to identify individuals even without explicit identifiers, revealing personal habits and routines.
assumptions: Location data contains unique patterns that can distinguish individuals from others.

title: Unauthorized Location Data Disclosure
description: Location history data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls or data breaches.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly enforced or data may be transmitted insecurely.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The system may store more location data than necessary for the map/history view function, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Full location history is stored rather than only necessary segments for the specific view.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: Malicious actors could impersonate legitimate users to access their location history through weak authentication or session hijacking.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to impersonation attacks.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Location Data
description: Processing location history may violate privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) requiring explicit consent and data protection measures.
assumptions: Location data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations.

title: Location Data Linkability to Child Identity
description: Location data shared with secondary guardian could be linked to identify the child's identity, home address, school, and daily routines through pattern analysis and cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: Secondary guardian has access to location data that can be correlated with other information to identify the child.

title: Direct Identifiability of Child's Location
description: The location data itself can directly identify the child's whereabouts, movements, and patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's daily life, home, school, and frequent locations.
assumptions: Location data contains precise geolocation information that can be used to identify the child's physical presence at specific locations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Location data shared with secondary guardian could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties if the guardian's account is compromised, or if the data is intercepted during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Secondary guardian account could be compromised, or data could be intercepted during transmission.

title: Location Data Integrity Compromise
description: Location data could be tampered with, falsified, or modified by malicious actors, leading to inaccurate location information being shared with the secondary guardian.
assumptions: Malicious actor has access to modify location data before it reaches the secondary guardian.

title: Usurpation of Location Access Rights
description: An unauthorized person could potentially access the location data intended for the secondary guardian, either through account takeover or by exploiting vulnerabilities in the access control mechanisms.
assumptions: Access control mechanisms have vulnerabilities that could be exploited to gain unauthorized access to location data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's live location to secondary guardian
description: The backend process shares the child's live location with the secondary guardian without proper verification of authorization or consent, potentially exposing sensitive personal data to unauthorized recipients.

title: Interception of live location data in transit
description: Live location data transmitted from the backend to the secondary guardian could be intercepted by malicious actors during transmission, leading to unauthorized access to real-time location information.

title: Linkability of location data to child's identity
description: The shared live location data can be linked to the child's identity, enabling tracking of the child's movements and potentially revealing patterns of behavior, school attendance, or home location.

title: Unawareness of data sharing scope by parents or child
description: Parents or the child may not be fully aware of the extent of data being shared with the secondary guardian, including duration, frequency, and specific data elements transmitted.

title: Secondary guardian misuses or over-discloses location data
description: The secondary guardian may misuse the received location data or further disclose it to third parties beyond the intended scope, violating the child's privacy expectations.

title: Data Leakage Through Improper Handling
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with external advertising partner may contain patterns that could be used to re-identify individual users or reveal sensitive behavioral patterns, even when aggregated.

title: Data Integrity Through Tampering
description: Analytics data transmitted to external partner could be intercepted, modified, or corrupted during transmission, potentially leading to inaccurate reporting or malicious manipulation of usage data.

title: Unintended Consequences Through Misuse
description: Advertising/analytics partner may use the shared analytics data for purposes beyond the agreed scope, such as building detailed user profiles, selling data to third parties, or making inferences about users not intended by the app developer.

title: Non-Compliance Through Regulatory Violations
description: Sharing user analytics with external partners may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, or user rights are not implemented.

title: Lack of Awareness Through Insufficient Information
description: Users may not be adequately informed about the extent of data sharing with advertising partners, including what data is collected, how it's used, and with whom it's shared.

title: Identification Through Data Correlation
description: Even aggregated analytics data could potentially be correlated with other data sources to identify individual users, especially if the app has unique usage patterns or if the aggregation is insufficient.

title: Location data identifies child's precise whereabouts
description: The child's current location data in the SOS/check-in message can be used to identify the child's exact physical location, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily routine, school, home, or other activities.

title: Location data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The child's location information could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through system vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls on the Mobile App Backend.

title: Location data linked with other data sources
description: The location data could be linked with other data about the child (e.g., school records, family information, device metadata) to create a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and activities.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: The system may collect more precise or frequent location data than necessary for the stated purpose of safety check-in/SOS, violating data minimization principles.

title: Non-compliance with children's data protection regulations
description: The processing of children's location data may not comply with GDPR-K or other data protection regulations specifically designed to protect minors' privacy rights.
